stem: A hybrid agent processes an incoming request. Place the following steps in the order they occur, from first to last.

options.text: The system attempts a fast reactive-style match against known patterns
The system detects low confidence or novelty in the fast-path result
The system escalates the request to a slower, deliberative reasoning process

explanation.why_correct: The hybrid pattern always tries the cheap, fast path first, then evaluates whether that attempt was confident/successful, and only escalates to the expensive deliberative path once insufficiency is detected -- in that strict order.
explanation.rule_of_thumb: Hybrid escalation always follows: try fast path, detect insufficiency, escalate to deliberation -- never the reverse order.

stem: Order the following tasks from MOST suited to a reactive architecture to MOST suited to a deliberative architecture.

options.text: Responding to a well-known greeting with a canned reply
Classifying a support ticket into one of a dozen known categories
Designing a multi-step project plan under several conflicting resource constraints

explanation.why_correct: A canned greeting reply is the simplest, most purely reactive case; ticket classification requires a bit more pattern discrimination but is still essentially a direct mapping; and multi-constraint project planning requires genuine lookahead and consequence-weighing, making it most suited to deliberative reasoning.
explanation.rule_of_thumb: Tasks requiring more lookahead and constraint-balancing are progressively better suited to deliberative architectures; simple, direct-mapping tasks are well suited to reactive ones.

stem: Match each agent architecture on the left to its defining characteristic on the right.

right.text: Maps current perception directly to action with no internal world model
Plans ahead using an internal model, weighing consequences of candidate actions
Combines a fast layer for common cases with selective escalation to a slower layer

explanation.why_correct: Each architecture has one clearly distinguishing trait: reactive agents map perception directly to action, deliberative agents plan ahead using an internal model, and hybrid agents combine both approaches with selective escalation.
explanation.rule_of_thumb: Reactive = direct mapping; deliberative = internal model plus lookahead; hybrid = both, combined via selective escalation.

stem: Match each scenario on the left to the architecture most appropriate for it on the right.

left.text: Real-time game NPC reacting to player movement within milliseconds
Multi-step logistics planning under several conflicting delivery constraints
A support system handling mostly routine tickets with occasional complex escalations

explanation.why_correct: The millisecond-response NPC task favors reactive design for speed, the multi-constraint logistics problem favors deliberative design for robustness, and the mixed routine/complex support system favors a hybrid design that escalates selectively.
explanation.rule_of_thumb: Match architecture to task shape: pure speed needs favor reactive, pure complexity favors deliberative, and a mix of both favors hybrid.
